resources.string: Race Marco Polo\'s road to the Khan and back.
Marco Hunt, a Kithe game. Build 0.3: solo on a plain board, placeholder art. No ads, no accounts, no data collected, no permissions.
Bulwark: perils hit you 2 weaker and you defend +2 (every other turn). Reach 1, strike +4. Your warm feels cold.
Trade: land on a traveller and swap a power-up instead of fighting. Reach 2, strike +3. Beasts hit you harder.
Divination: name two empty squares, learn which is nearer Marco. Reach 4, strike +1.
Volley: two attacks in one action (reach 3, strike +2). Leap and Falcon suit you.
Your turn — roll %1$d. Tap a lit square.
%1$s is frozen and loses the turn.
The Land of Darkness hides your signal.
Who is Marco? You can accuse only once.
No — %1$s is not Marco. Your accusation is spent.
The Spyglass caught an echo! Your earlier signals may have lied.
The Spyglass sees no echo: your signal is true.
The Compass: Marco is %1$d rows from you.
The Compass: Marco is %1$d columns from you.
The first square is nearer to Marco.
The second square is nearer to Marco.
The Khan\'s astrologers speak: near the %1$s, Marco walked; now he is about %2$d squares from it.
Marco escaped: nobody found him in %1$d rounds.
Marco was %1$s. He cast %2$d traps and gifts and planted %3$d false signals, called echoes (a Spyglass caught %4$d). Dangers that hit you: %5$d from his traps, %6$d from bad luck.
the Tree of the Golden Fleece
You are a traveller on an old map. One of the other travellers is secretly Marco. Find him: land on his square, or accuse him — once.
That colour is your temperature. HOT: Marco is close. WARM: middle. COLD: far. It is measured from you to Marco — compare it with where each traveller stands. The ticks show who fits.
Each new signal clears more travellers. The one who keeps fitting is your Marco… unless he set an echo (a decoy). A Spyglass sees through echoes.
Decorated squares may hide a gift, a trap — or nothing. Marco also hides traps in them.
Landing on a traveller who is not Marco starts a fight — and proves he is not Marco.
When only one traveller fits, tap Accuse. You get one accusation, so be sure.
Help with the ticks: first turns only on Wayfarer, never on Master.
where Marco used to watch the falcons
where Marco used to rest in the shade
where Marco used to light a candle
Near %1$s there is %2$s %3$s. Now he is some %4$d squares from it.
The stars say: by %1$s stands %2$s %3$s. Today the traveller is about %4$d squares away from it.
Seek %1$s, and beside it %2$s %3$s. %4$d squares, more or less, now lie between him and it.
Long-press a square to read the map.
A riddle from the Khan\'s astrologers

We read the stars for you all night, and they puzzled us. They spoke of a traveller born on a day that is not the birthday — and yet it counts. The traveller asked for a game, and the game came wrapped in parchment with a red bow. The traveller walks inside maps no one has drawn yet, and hunts a man who hides among friends. Who is this traveller? We argued until dawn. Then we wrote one word on the scroll, and it was the name of whoever now holds this phone. Happy birthday, traveller. The stars insist it counts.
Paintings made with Canva AI (owned by the maker under Canva\'s AI Product Terms).
Board set: it is in front of you.
Walk to the lit square, then tap I\'m here.
The camera shows the board on the ground. Marco Hunt uses the camera only for that, and saves nothing.
On this phone you stay in one spot and your piece walks for you. Face the way you want the board and tap Set board: it appears in front of you.
No camera: the map board still works.
Pick two objects on the ground, one for corner A and one for corner B, at least 2 metres apart. Walk to A and tap Set board, then to B and tap it again. The little map shows both corners and your ★.
Move the phone slowly so it can see the ground…
Stand at the first-corner object and tap Set board
Corner 1 saved. Now walk to the far-corner object and tap Set board.
You are only %1$d cm from the first corner. Walk at least 2 metres away, then tap Set board again.
The phone thinks you are on square %1$d,%2$d. Walk to the lit square, or tap I\'m here again to confirm.
Walk the old map. Tap to hunt.
The camp is struck: the hunt goes on where you left it.
You can only walk to a gold square: up to %1$d steps, no diagonals.
The cold still holds you: you miss this turn.
You rest and get a heart back: %1$s
You rest. Your hearts are already full.
Your skill is resting. Ready again in round %1$d.
This skill works by itself when it is ready: you don\'t need to tap anything.
No actions left this turn. Walk to end your turn.
Nobody is close enough to attack: you reach %1$d squares.
Each traveller can accuse only once per game. Keep hunting: you can still find Marco by landing on his square.
Leap! %1$d extra steps: you can now walk exactly %2$d.
Shield raised: the next danger can\'t hurt you.
Tap the signal to read what it means.
Marco is close: %1$d squares or fewer from you.
Marco is at middle distance: %1$d to %2$d squares from you.
Marco is far: more than %1$d squares from you.
(As a Knight you feel warm as cold.)

After each walk you get a signal: how far you are from Marco, in steps with no diagonals. Warmer means you got closer, colder means further. He creeps around slowly. Once in a game he may send a false signal, so trust several, not one.
Warmer than last turn: you got closer.
Colder than last turn: you got farther.
The Land of Darkness hides signals for a while. They come back by themselves.
The Falcon flies toward Marco. It is used up now.
Count the steps along that line from your square. The Compass is used up now.
A decoration: it hides a helper, a danger, or nothing. Step on it to find out.
%1$s stepped on the Spotlight square: %1$s is Marco! Now catch them.
One square on the map is the Spotlight. If Marco steps on it, everyone sees who he is.
A draw: nobody moves, nothing is lost.
They had nothing to take, so you get an extra action next turn.
They are pushed back and lose a heart.
And now you know: %1$s is not Marco (✗).

Both roll a die. The attacker adds a strike bonus (Knight +4, Traveler +3, Mongol +2, Magus +1). A Leap or Shield that suits your class adds +2 and is used up. Landing on a traveller starts a fight too.
Darkness falls: your next %1$d signal(s) will be hidden.
The cold grips you: you miss your next turn.
It throws you up to %1$d squares away.
Your Shield stopped it! The Shield is used up.
It couldn\'t hurt you this time: your class is strong against it.
Decorations can hide dangers. A Shield stops one.
Hearts: with all of them you can hear the Oracle. Rest (stay a whole turn) gives one back.
opened a decoration and found a helper 🎁
It is in your sac now (bottom of the screen). Tap it on your turn, before you walk. Long-press it to read this again.
It is in your sac and works by itself.
The Khan\'s astrologers live on this square. Stand here with all your hearts and they read you a riddle about where Marco walked.
Leap: use it before you walk. You get extra steps this turn.
Shield: it works by itself. It stops the next danger, or a traveller taking your helper. Then it is used up.
Spyglass: Marco can fake your signal with an echo (a decoy). The Spyglass shows whether he is doing it now, and breaks it.
Falcon: tells you which way Marco is: north, east, south or west.
Compass: tells you exactly how many rows (or columns) Marco is from you.
This is Marco! Land on his square to catch him.
Fits your last signal: could be Marco.
Doesn\'t fit your last signal: probably not Marco (unless an echo fooled you).

You are the ★. Marco is hiding somewhere on this board, and you can\'t see him.\n\nAfter each walk, the signal says HOT, WARM or COLD. Follow it and land on his square to win. Two other travellers are hunting him too.
The red die is how far you can walk: up to %1$d steps, no diagonals. The gold squares show where. Tap one.\n\nIf you have a helper, tap it first.
Now the other travellers walk, one by one. The banner on the map says what each one did.

Decorations (cactus, jar, rock, wheat) all look alike: one may hide a helper, a danger, the Oracle or nothing. You only find out by stepping on it. The gold tiles and round marks are places on the map: they hide nothing, and the Oracle\'s riddles talk about them. Long-press any square to read it.
Only %1$s fits your last signal. If earlier signals agree, tap Accuse and pick them. You get one try, so be sure.
Look up often and watch where you walk.
You start on row %1$d, column %2$d: the ★ on the map.
Go to corner A on the little map and tap Set board.
Now walk to corner B and tap Set board. You are %1$s m from A (at least 2 m).
You are outside the board. Go to: row %1$d, column %2$d.
You are on your square: row %1$d, column %2$d ✓
You: row %1$d, column %2$d → Go to: row %3$d, column %4$d
Your piece: row %1$d, column %2$d. Stay where you are: tap a gold square and it walks there.
You rolled %1$d. Set the board first.
Marco was hiding on row %1$d, column %2$d.
%1$s had a %2$s. It is yours now.
%1$s\'s Shield stopped you taking anything. The Shield is used up.
%1$s landed on you and took your %2$s.
%1$s landed on you, but your Shield stopped them. It is used up.
Land on a traveller and you take one of their helpers.
Hunting Marco too, %1$d steps from you. Land on them to take one of their helpers.
Raiders call down a darkness by enchantment and fall on the caravan.
Up here the cold is so deep that fire burns weak and gives little heat.
In the night, voices call you by name and lead you away from the road.
The last of the desert: voices you know call from the dark, the wrong way.
You leave Venice ⚓ in the corner. The road spirals to the Khan 👑 in the middle. Bring back his treasure 💰: first one home wins.
Roll, then tap a gold square. You may walk up to your roll, forward or back.
The Khan sees nobody without 3 gifts 🎁. Stop exactly on one to take it: walking past leaves it. One per land.
Each colour is a land. Rivals take gifts too, and a taken gift is gone.
Red bars join a ring to the next one, skipping almost a whole lap. But 2 times in 3 the pass fails: you lose a turn and are thrown back 6 squares.
Squares you can only reach through a pass turn red. A Tablet of Gold 🥇 saves you once.
On the way home, anyone with 3 gifts can land on you and try to take your treasure: it works 1 time in 2. You can rob them the same way.
If you are robbed, you lose a turn and go back to the Khan for another. You can\'t rob the one who just robbed you.
Carry the treasure home to Venice ⚓. Rivals can rob you.
Go back to the Khan 👑 for another treasure, or land on someone who has one.
You have your 3 gifts. Get to the Khan 👑.
Gifts: %1$d of 3. Stop on a 🎁 in a land you have none from.
You rolled %1$d. Gold is safe, red is through a pass. Your own square means stay.
You can\'t reach that square. Tap a gold or red one.
It skips almost a whole lap, but it fails 2 times in 3.
If it fails, you lose a turn and are thrown back 6 squares.
You got through! Almost a whole lap saved.
You show the Tablet of Gold and pass safely. The Tablet is used up.
The pass failed: thrown back 6 squares, and you lose your next turn.
You now have %1$d of 3 gifts for the Khan.
You can take one gift from each land.
The Khan\'s safe-conduct. It works by itself: it stops one failed pass or one robbery.
The Khan\'s couriers lend you a fresh horse: 3 extra steps on your next roll.
The Khan takes your gifts and hands you his treasure 💰. Now race home to Venice ⚓.
The arrows on the road now point home. Watch for rivals coming the other way.
You took the treasure from the %1$s. Run for Venice ⚓.
The %1$s held on to the treasure.
The %1$s showed a Tablet of Gold. It is used up now.
You lose your next turn. Go back to the Khan for another; you don\'t need gifts this time.
The %1$s tried to rob you and failed.
The %1$s tried to rob you. Your Tablet of Gold stopped it, and it is used up.
You stay where you are while the others move.
They\'re heading home now, and may cross your path. With 3 gifts you can land on them and try to rob them.
You won the race in %1$d rounds.
The race took %1$d rounds. Next time, take the treasure off them.
A gift, but you can\'t take it now
